item.title: From Purity Rings to Shooting Your Dog: How Christian Womanhood Went MAGA
item.description: Growing up in the 1990s meant purity rings and Josh Harris books — now the loudest Christian women are countering 'toxic empathy' and shooting dogs.

item.title: In Minnesota, US cardinals and pope’s ambassador decry mass deportations and call for reconciliation
item.description: ST PAUL, Minn. (AP) — In St. Paul on Friday, Cardinal Robert McElroy of Washington addressed growing concerns with immigration enforcement while highlighting the need to be peacemakers on the polarizing issue after a Mass for migrants he celebrated with his fellow prelates and the Twin Cities’ archbishop.

item.title: A new Gallup poll shows how Americans’ sympathies have shifted in the Israeli-Palestinian conflict
item.description: That shift accelerated during the war in Gaza. Three years ago, 54% of Americans sympathized more with the Israelis, compared with 31% for the Palestinians.

item.title: In ‘El Mencho’s’ last redoubt, a crucifix, saint candles and a handwritten psalm
item.description: The house inside an exclusive subdivision in southern Jalisco state contained a crucifix, as well as a makeshift altar with religious figurines of Our Lady of Guadalupe, Saint Jude Thaddeus and Saint Charbel Makhlouf, along with votive candles with images of saints.

item.title: Hundreds of corrections being issued for Texas’ Bible-infused curriculum
item.description: The curriculum in what is known as the “Bluebonnet” textbook is among Republican-led efforts in the U.S. to incorporate more religious teaching into classrooms.

item.title: Impulsive kings and random chance: Purim’s parallels to our political moment
item.description: While Trump wages his war of choice on the thinnest of pretexts, the Jewish calendar is focusing on the vanity of human power and the amorality with which it is exercised.

item.title: Why A War With Iran Means Confronting Radical Evil
item.description: For Jews observing Purim, the timing of the attack on Iran is uncanny. The lessons are sobering.

item.title: Iranian evangelicals are staying put, tentative but hopeful, says pastor
item.description: 'With this death of the supreme leader, everybody is firstly happy and hopeful but are still asking 'What's next?'' said Hormoz Shariat, who runs a streaming ministry for Iranian Christians.

item.title: How the Book of Esther echoes through 17th-century Netherlands to this day
item.description: RALEIGH, N.C. (RNS) — Since its inclusion in the Hebrew Bible, the Book of Esther has been embraced in different ways and in different times by Jews and Christians around the world.
